searchText: <@!301186049323958275> I took heed of your preference for a super minimal user experience and outlined a proforma for a prototypical wallet interface https://perama-v.github.io/cairo/ethereum/wallet-design I'm not building a wallet, it is just an interest. Let me know of any suggestions or changes and I can update it It also includes some brief notes to implementers directing them how to best use <@!202397237962211328> 's great feeHistory API I think I would use the terminology "maximum transaction fee" rather than "transaction fee" for the simple interface. Don't call it a `tip`! It gives the user the wrong impression about it and it is inconsistent with the agreed messaging we are trying to get across. "Gas Premium" is what it is being called now. I also am *personally* on a crusade against Gwei, for the same reason I'm against feet, miles, and the entire imperial measurement system. It is ridiculous and we have international standards (SI prefixes) for a reason. I understand that I'm losing this war, just like I'm losing the war against the imperial measurement system in the US. 😖 > m times basefee (refundable). Consider instead for clarity: > m times basefee (excess refunded). It isn't obvious in the UI that clicking the "back" button will save changes you have made. The UX makes me think that only "send" will save changes. ~~You don't mention how you are calculating the various gas premium suggestions.~ Your sample numbers are *insane*. I would expect more like `[low 1] [medium 2] [high 5]` Thank thanks thanks! 2.5e-9 rather than 2.5 Gwei? `2.5 nanoeth` Like a sane person. 😉 I like it, yotta tell more people I tell everyone who will listen. It is a big part of the reason I have no friends. All suggestions have now been included. 👍 Open to further feedback <@!301186049323958275> i am intrigued, what do you think should be used instead of Gwei? would love a 101 on SI as it related to Ethereum potential subunits Standard SI prefixes, like nanoeth. Or attoeth. Ethereum being the name of the unit (like `meter`), and everything just being an SI prefix added onto that (like nanometer). what positives do you think that will serve? like why do you see that as a better alternative to the existing? I love it. Pick one unit and stick to it 1 ether 1 nanoether 1 attoether Or use wei 1 exawei 1 gigawei 1 wei But don't use both and have them "mash" in the middle One example might be that the first thing a new user learns is that there is a currency, ether. Then comes gas And then comes the word gwei, which leads to wei. That leads to the redefinition of ether in terms of wei, undermining the very first bedrock of knowledge they learned (there is no ether, it's just bundles of wei) Lower barrier of entry to new users into the ecosystem. I would say that the vast majority of users don't realize that `gwei` is really just "small amounts of ETH". They think `gwei` is some kind of magical gas unit. If we called it `nanoeth`, I think instead the vast majority of users (anyone educated on SI prefixes, which is everyone but people from a few holdout countries and anyone with a science/math education within those countries) would intuitively understand that gas is priced in ETH if it were priced as `nanoeth`. If you denominate in `wei` you run out of prefixes on the top end. 😄 Yotta to atto gives you a really nice range centered around `ether`, which is the primary measurement of the currency of Ethereum (not `wei`). Yeah totally in favour of ether rather than wei Here's how it could play out, wait for a protocol change where every wallet and interface is changing their UI all at the same time. Then form a style guide and one-image it (ultrasound money style) for memefication. Then spark a rally to make together for the upgrade If only there was such an opportunity... I support you leading the charge on this <@743395542196944977>. Good luck! was Gwei ever referred to as "Shannon", as this website claims? https://gwei.io/ (I like SI units too btw... but it's true many users have an intuition for what a Gwei is and not necessarily a nanoeth...) But nanoeth is the same as Gwei. Could perhaps also write it as nETH? Let's lean into the culture already built: 1 ether = 1 gigaGwei Case closed! GGwei gg (for when the fees are too high) I think it would be `Ggwei` since it seems most people don't understand the `g` is a prefix. But then it's giga giga watt euler imaginary Watt would be capital W though 🤔 one crusade at a time, Micah 😛 interesting - Radar relay also runs https://weth.io/ i didn't know they also ran gwei.io wonder what the traffic is on these sites

excerpts.content: Don't call it a `tip`!  It gives the user the wrong impression about it and it is inconsistent with the agreed messaging we are trying to get across.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: "Gas Premium" is what it is being called now.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus

It is ridiculous and we have international standards (SI prefixes) for a reason.  I understand that I'm losing this war, just like I'm losing the war against the imperial measurement system in the US.  😖

excerpts.author: perama
excerpts.content:
I love it. Pick one unit and stick to it

1 ether
1 nanoether
1 attoether

Or use wei
1 exawei
1 gigawei 
1 wei

But don't use both and have them "mash" in the middle

excerpts.author: perama
excerpts.content:
One example might be that the first thing a new user learns is that there is a currency, ether.

Then comes gas

And then comes the word gwei, which leads to wei. That leads to the redefinition of ether in terms of wei, undermining the very first bedrock of knowledge they learned (there is no ether, it's just bundles of wei)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Lower barrier of entry to new users into the ecosystem.  I would say that the vast majority of users don't realize that `gwei` is really just "small amounts of ETH".  They think `gwei` is some kind of magical gas unit.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If we called it `nanoeth`, I think instead the vast majority of users (anyone educated on SI prefixes, which is everyone but people from a few holdout countries and anyone with a science/math education within those countries) would intuitively understand that gas is priced in ETH if it were priced as `nanoeth`.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If you denominate in `wei` you run out of prefixes on the top end.  😄  Yotta to atto gives you a really nice range centered around `ether`, which is the primary measurement of the currency of Ethereum (not `wei`).

excerpts.author: perama
excerpts.content: Yeah totally in favour of ether rather than wei
